In high school, he was selected as a [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] and [[California Mr. Basketball]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA Bruins]], earning all-freshman honors in the [[Pac-12 Conference]] in his only season. He was selected by the [[Charlotte Hornets]] in the second round of the [[2023 NBA draft]]. ==Early life== Bailey was born in [[New Orleans]], Louisiana. He is the son of Johanna Leia (original surname Edelberg), a [[social media influencer]] and former [[Ford Models|Ford]] model, and former [[NFL]] [[Indianapolis Colts]] wide receiver [[Aaron Bailey (American football)|Aaron Bailey]]; the two eventually split.{{Cite web|url=https://www.usmagazine.com/celebrity-news/pictures/amari-bailey-mom/|title=Who Is Amari Bailey's Mom? 6 Things to Know About Johanna Leia|date=September 2, 2022}}{{Cite web|url=https://forward.com/news/sports/551429/amari-bailey-jewish-nba-draft/|title=UCLA's Bailey set to join NBA's Jewish ranks|date=June 21, 2023|website=The Forward|author=Louis Keene}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.timesofisrael.com/jewish-guard-amari-bailey-drafted-41st-overall-by-charlotte-hornets/|title=Jewish guard Amari Bailey drafted 41st overall by Charlotte Hornets |work= The Times of Israel|author=Jacob Gurvis}}{{cite web|title=Amari Bailey|publisher=UCLA Athletics|url=https://uclabruins.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/amari-bailey/11347|access-date=November 13, 2022}} Edelberg is Jewish, as is Amari.{{Cite web|url=https://www.jpost.com/j-spot/article-747488 |title=Jewish player Amari Bailey drafted 41st overall by the Charlotte Hornets|date=June 24, 2023|website=The Jerusalem Post}} Bailey grew up in [[Chicago]], Illinois, and was raised by Edelberg.{{cite web |last1=Yapkowitz |first1=David |title=Amari Bailey: "I want to be the best player I can be in high school" |url=https://www.marsreel.com/amari-bailey-i-want-to-be-the-best-player-i-can-be-in-high-school/ |website=Mars Reel |access-date=July 17, 2021 |date=May 20, 2019}}{{cite news|first=Marc. was selected by the [[Charlotte Hornets]] in the second round of the [[2023 NBA draft]] with the 41st overall pick. On July 14, 2023, he signed a [[two-way contract]] with the Hornets,{{cite web|title=Charlotte Hornets Sign Amari Bailey To Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/charlotte-hornets-sign-amari-bailey-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=July 14, 2023|access-date=July 14, 2023}} which he said was worth $565,000. Playing for the Hornets in the 2023 [[NBA Summer League]], he averaged nine points in 16 minutes per game. At 19 years of age, he was the 10th-youngest player in the league.{{cite news|first=Sarah|last=Effress|title=Amari Bailey excited about future with Hornets: 'There's a lot to look forward to here.'|url=https://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/article278068972.html|newspaper=The Charlotte Observer|date=August 14, 2023|access-date=October 26, 2023}}{{cite web|first=Dionysis|last=Aravantinos|title=The youngest players in 2023 Summer League|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/youngest-players-2023-summer-league-092127476.html|work=Yahoo Sports|date=July 7, 2023|access-date=October 21, 2024}} On November 17, 2023, he made his [[G-League]] debut with the [[Greensboro Swarm]], and scored 26 points.{{cite web|first=Cody|last=Taylor|title=Amari Bailey scores 26 points, Leaky Black nears triple-double in G League debuts|url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/2023/11/18/hornets-amari-bailey-leaky-black-g-league-swarm/|website=USAToday.com|date=November 18, 2023|access-date=October 21, 2024}} Bailey made his NBA debut on November 12, 2023, for the Hornets against the [[New York Knicks]].[https://www.nba.com/gamenotes/hornets.pdfl "Game Notes,"] NBA.com. On September 21, 2024, Bailey signed with the [[Brooklyn Nets]],{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Amari Bailey|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-sign-amari-bailey|website=NBA.com|date=September 21, 2024|access-date=September 22, 2024}} but was waived on October 19.{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets Waive Amari Bailey and Killian Hayes|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-waive-amari-bailey-and-killian-hayes|website=NBA.com|date=October 19, 2024|access-date=October 21, 2024}} Eight days later, he joined the [[Long Island Nets]].{{cite tweet|author=Long Island Nets|title=Our official training camp roster 🔥 #StrongIsland 💪|number=1850674269581197342|user=LongIslandNets|date=October 27, 2024|access-date=October 28, 2024}} On December 30, 2024, Bailey was traded to the [[Iowa Wolves]] in a three-team trade involving the [[Stockton Kings]] with Stockton receiving [[Chasson Randle]] from Iowa and Long Island acquiring [[Drew Timme]] from Stockton.{{cite web|title=Wolves Acquire Guard Amari Bailey in 3-Team Trade|url=https://iowa.gleague.nba.com/news/wolves-acquire-guard-amari-bailey-in-3-team-trade|website=NBA.com|date=December 30, 2024|access-date=December 30, 2024}} ==National team career== Bailey represented the [[United States men's national under-17 basketball team|United States]] at the [[2019 FIBA Under-16 Americas Championship]] in Brazil.
